Active learning for molecular property prediction

Abstract
Active learning strategies are applied to reduce labeling cost in molecular property prediction. We benchmark on QM9 and a custom dataset.

Introduction
Modern molecular machine learning increasingly relies on labels that are expensive to acquire, motivating careful sample selection.

Methods
We compare uncertainty-based, diversity-based, and committee-based active learning strategies across a 1024-dimensional Morgan fingerprint representation. All experiments are run on a single workstation; no robotic platform is involved.

Results
On QM9 we achieve 95% of full-data performance using only 18% of labels.

Discussion
These results suggest active learning can substantially reduce computational cost for property prediction tasks.

Acknowledgements
We thank the German Research Foundation (DFG) and TU Munich for funding this work. We acknowledge support from the Bavarian State Ministry of Science and the Arts.

References
1. Reker, D.; Schneider, G. Active-Learning Strategies in Computer-Assisted Drug Discovery. Drug Discovery Today 2015.
